hypothesis: When learned redundant clauses cease being reused while propagation efficiency or clause quality deteriorates, a local restart-intensity change at 2048 conflicts may improve PAR-2.
native_measure: Kissat solver->statistics.clauses_used incremented in deduce.c mark_clause_as_used for redundant reason clauses; locally read at conflicts 256/512/1024; clauses_learned and propagation/glue from frozen R16 checkpoints.
metric: Uprev=(used_512-used_256)/(1+learned_512-learned_256); Urecent=(used_1024-used_512)/(1+learned_1024-learned_512); prop per conflict and glue ratio are secondary. Clauses_used is an aggregate reuse proxy, not direct proof of clause quality.

validation.primary: 60 brand new random3_test CNFs, native r20_local50 vs same patched binary monitor, 95% stratified-by-n formula bootstrap CI
secondary: forced50 and R16 baselines; original Kissat/V15.3.1 references
trigger/actual restart parity, missed large gains and >2x regressions
SAT witnesses, UNSAT status agreement with original; independent UNSAT proofs not provided
SHA-exclusive formula, same runner/core, same preintervention checkpoints
R20_TRACE used and improved counters at 256/512/1024 and R20_DECISION verified independently in Python
validation.confidence: An all-negative CI for gain or no activations is a negative result; no claimed law or world record.

freeze: No threshold tuning after observing R20 development or holdout. R19 retrospective examples are diagnostic only. Promotion prohibited without verified benefit on unseen test.
